channel.title: The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Center For Michigan | Bridge Magazine (thecenterformichigan.net)

item.title: Desperate for doctors: Michigan looks to expand who can provide care
item.description: Lawmakers are trying to ease dangerous short-staffing in health care by tweaking laws — expanding the ability of some mid-level practitioners and, in some cases, creating new types of workers.

item.title: Michigan: Macomb clerk’s noncitizen voter claims overstated
item.description: The Macomb County clerk had flagged 15 names. Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson says there's evidence one voted, but some are citizens.

item.title: Bridge Michigan News Quiz: Jan. 30: Who loves winter?
item.description: It’s almost Groundhog Day. Will it see its shadow? One thing is sure: there’s at least six more weeks of amazing trivia about Michigan news.

item.title: 4 years after Oxford school shooting, families still await answers from state
item.description: The Oxford High shooter is behind bars. Families of the four students killed in 2021 are waiting for a state review into how he went undetected.

item.title: Fact check: Are regulations to blame for rising Michigan house costs?
item.description: Candidates for governor want to tame bureaucracy to incentivize affordable housing, but there are many other reasons why housing is slightly more expensive in Michigan than nearby states.

item.title: Michigan license plate cameras face backlash: Big help, or Big Brother?
item.description: Privacy advocates are raising red flags over Flock cameras used in more than 125 Michigan cities and counties. But police say they help solve crimes. ‘We do not spy on residents,' said one chief.

item.title: Dana Nessel becomes debt collector as Michigan seeks $24M from Gotion
item.description: The attorney general is getting involved as the state’s feud with the failed battery plant plan takes another turn.

item.title: Snowmobile race coming to the Soo. Meet the Michigan ‘troll’ in charge
item.description: Ric Federau is the longest serving chair of the International 500 snowmobile race in Sault Ste. Marie, but he’s from south of the Mackinac Bridge.

item.title: Michigan quietly kills effort to restructure mental health care system
item.description: The decision follows a judge’s order to block the state’s request for proposal. The state says its aim in seeking bidders was to introduce ‘consumer choice’ to the Medicaid-backed system.

item.title: In Michigan Senate race, Dems battle for bucks as Mike Rogers builds war chest
item.description: Six months from the primary and with no clear frontrunner for the Democratic nomination, fundraising remains tight in Michigan’s closely-watched US Senate race.
